question: On a real Huya live room, does the shipped extension pause without a playback readback mismatch, and do its volume and the site's own volume slider follow each other in both directions?
head: 332fe7a
commit: 332fe7a fix(spectra): sync huya native playback and volume controls
repairState: The repair was first probed and verified in a working tree on top of 91ad0f63, then committed as 332fe7a. The production artifact was rebuilt again from that committed HEAD and the same content-runtime.js SHA-256 was obtained byte for byte; the two official acceptance rounds below were re-run against that committed-HEAD build.

artifact.rebuiltFrom: committed HEAD 332fe7a; identical to the working-tree build used by the intermediate rounds
artifact.finalRefactor: SCTRL-003 requires exactly one canonical element.volume writer. The mirror alignment was moved from site-native-control-surface.ts into native-media-executor.ts without changing behaviour; the final four real-site rounds below and the full smoke run use this final artifact, and the two OFFICIAL rounds rebuilt it from the committed HEAD.

site.scope: anonymous public Huya live room, 2026-11-14 build of vplayer.js

nativeWidgets.playPause: #player-btn (player-pause-btn / 暂停观看 -> player-play-btn / 开始观看)
nativeWidgets.volumeBar: .sound-bar (width in px is the site's own level)

site.ownership: The site's vplayer.js owns playback state and the audible volume level. The media element's paused / volume properties are mirrors the player writes, not the source of truth.

method: Rebuild the production extension from the working tree, load it into the specified local Chrome via CDP, and use only real viewer input for the site side: scroll the control bar into view, move the pointer over #player-wrap and #player-sound-btn, drag .sound-btn with the mouse, open the trusted toolbar action popup with Extensions.triggerAction, click .btn-pause and drive .vol-slider with real keyboard input. Oracles are the shipped control snapshot in chrome.storage.local, the action badge, the popup slider, and the site's own DOM. Observation-only probes additionally wrap HTMLMediaElement.prototype.play/pause and the volume descriptor in both page and isolated worlds to record call stacks, and sample tab-capture RMS for audibility.

assertions: the site's own #player-btn and .sound-bar widgets exist before any gesture is used as parity evidence
a real drag of the site's own volume handle moves element.volume below 0.45 and the shipped volumeBase follows within 3 units
the extension pause ACK is phase applied with lastError null and the site's #player-btn title becomes 开始观看
a second pause press resumes with an applied ACK and lastError null
real arrow keys on the popup slider to 70 make the snapshot, the site's element volume, the site's filled bar, the badge and the popup slider agree

runs.label: official gated real-site round, intermediate artifact
working-tree final artifact round 1 (before the SCTRL-003 commit)
working-tree final artifact round 2 (before the SCTRL-003 commit)

assertionsProven: Seven real-site rounds agree on the same numbers in both directions. The two OFFICIAL rounds rebuilt the production artifact from the committed HEAD 332fe7a, obtained the same content-runtime.js SHA-256, and each passed 16 expect() after two added widget-existence assertions.
The pause button no longer produces readback-mismatch; the shipped playing field is applied with actual false and lastError null, and Huya's own button changes to 开始观看.
The site's native slider owns the audible level; the extension now drives that slider and reports the site's own level to the popup, snapshot and badge.

pauseRootCause.symptom: Playback readback mismatch: requested playing=false; after write=false; stable=true, on every pause press

lastError.message: Playback readback mismatch: requested playing=false; after write=false; stable=true

pauseRootCause.pageWorldCaller: prototype.play called from https://a.msstatic.com/huya/h5player/room/2611111128/vplayer.js (recorded in the same room in a later probe)
pauseRootCause.explanation: A raw element.pause() from the isolated content world pauses the media element, but Huya's own state machine still says watching and calls play() again about 30 ms later. writePlaybackWithStableAck waits for a stable readback, sees true, and necessarily throws.

volumeRootCause.siteToExtensionBefore: A real drag of .sound-btn from 0.5 to 0.12 moved element.volume to 0.12 and the extension already followed to 12 through the native volumechange observation (bar 43.5px -> 12.5px, badge 12). This direction was never a Huya acceptance item.
volumeRootCause.extensionToSiteBefore: The plugin slider went through documentOutput / Capture: snapshot and badge showed 70 while element.volume stayed 0.5 and .sound-bar stayed 43.5px. The site's own UI never moved.

domMirrorExperiment.conclusion: Writing element.volume changes only the DOM mirror; the site's own bar and the site's audible level do not follow. It cannot bridge the two UIs.

audibilityOracle.conclusion: Huya's own slider controls the real audible output, so the extension must move that slider rather than only its own processor gain.

syntheticInputOracle.world: isolated content script (the product's own execution world), plus a page-world control
syntheticInputOracle.conclusion: Synthetic MouseEvent input dispatched on the site's own widgets reaches Huya's handlers from the isolated world; no page-global player API and no CDP input are required in the product.

repair: site-native-control-surface.ts: discover the site's own play/pause button and volume track observation-first; a missing or unresponsive control is a no-op and the standard DOM writer stays authoritative.

site-native-control-surface.ts: projectSiteNativePlayback clicks the site's own button before writePlaybackWithStableAck, so the player's internal state agrees with the element and the pause is not replayed.

site-native-control-surface.ts: projectSiteNativeVolume drives the site's own track with bounded synthetic pointer/mouse input, reads the site's filled bar as the physical witness, returns the level it actually reached or null, and never writes element.volume.

native-media-executor.ts: route playing and documentOutput volumeBase through those projections; align the DOM mirror here as the single canonical volume writer required by SCTRL-003; keep the Capture processor at unity when the site owns the level; publish the witnessed site level as the displayed volumeBase while retaining the runtime field-state contract (strategy capture / coverage opaque).
audio-runtime-control-delegate.ts: separate the gain input from the displayed level with a siteNativeLevel witness, so a passive read does not report the processor's 100 as the viewer's volume.
test/site-native-control-surface.spec.ts and test/smoke/huya-native-parity.spec.ts: 5 unit cases (no-op, calibration, canonical-writer boundary) and a gated real-site two-way acceptance case.
findings.canonicalWriterRefactor: The first verify run reported SCTRL-003: unowned volume writer at site-native-control-surface.ts. The mirror write was moved into native-media-executor.ts (the existing single canonical writer) and a unit case now asserts the projection leaves the mirror alone. The gate was not loosened and no baseline was changed.
rejected: Writing element.volume to bridge the site UI: proven not to move the site bar.
Only changing the Capture processor gain: the site UI stays at its old number while the extension shows another.
Using a page-global player API: the diagnostic probe found no usable volume/play method pair on the exposed globals.

Overriding the RPC read with the site bar width directly in NativeMediaExecutor.read(): it broke the popup's field-state contract (Control state unavailable / aria-pressed mixed) and was reverted in favour of the delegate witness.

sitePhysicalCeiling.decision: The site's 90px track and 10px handle make 0.944 its physical maximum for a track click. The extension reports 94 honestly to the snapshot, popup and badge; it does not claim 100 while the site shows 94. A request of 30 reaches 0.3 / 27px / 30 exactly.

boundaries.fallback: If no site-native control is found, or three bounded calibration passes cannot reach the requested level within tolerance, the projection returns null and the previous routing is kept unchanged. Ordinary dom-native pages are not affected.
boundaries.boost: boost > 100 still goes through the verified Capture processor gain; a site UI cannot display a value above its own maximum.
boundaries.rmsAfterRepair: The separate tab-capture RMS sampler cannot open a second stream while the extension already owns an active capture ('Cannot capture a tab with an active stream.'). The audibility oracle above was sampled before the extension held that capture.
